description: The MET tower will have a total height of approximately 328 feet (100 meters) above mean sea level.
context_quote: The overall height of the MET tower structure (mast & foundation) will be approximately 328 feet (~100 m) above the mean sea level.

description: The MET tower platform deck will be approximately 3,000 square feet (279 square meters) in size.
context_quote: The platform deck supporting the mast will be approximately 3,000 square feet (279 square meters) with the upper access platform located at a Top of Grating (TOG) of approximately 70 feet (21.3 meters).

description: The bottom of the MET tower steel will be located at approximately 68 feet (20.7 meters) to clear the 1,000-year crest elevation.
context_quote: The Bottom of Steel (BOS) will be located at approximately 68 feet (20.7 meters) in order to clear the 1,000 year crest elevation.

description: The MET tower mast and platform deck will be equipped with safety lighting, markings, and signal equipment per FAA and USCG requirements.
context_quote: Both the mast and the platform deck will be equipped with the proper safety lighting, markings and signal equipment per Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and United States Coast Guard (USCG) Private Aids to Navigation (PATON) requirements.

description: The oceanographic measurement package will be tethered to a foundation pile with an offset of approximately 10 feet (3 meters).
context_quote: The sea-bed mounted oceanographic data gathering package will be housed in an industry standard trawl resistant bottom mount with a bottom APE of approximately 58" long x 58" wide x 21" deep (147 cm x 147 cm x 53 cm). The package will be tethered to a foundation pile with an offset of approximately 10 feet (3 meters).

description: The MET tower will be serviced via small (25-foot) vessels operating from Ocean City, Maryland approximately two times per month.
context_quote: Approximately two trips per month via small (25 ft) vessels, likely operating from Ocean City, will be required to service the MET tower during operation.

description: The MET tower construction and decommissioning will require a lift boat, materials barge, and crew/supply boat making a total of 14 trips over a two-week period.
context_quote: Several trips over an approximately two-week period would be required to transport construction crews and materials to the MET tower site.

description: Pile driving activities for MET tower installation will implement a 'soft start' procedure to allow marine mammals and sea turtles to vacate the area.
context_quote: A 'soft start' must be implemented at the beginning of each pile installation in order to provide additional protection to marine mammals and sea turtles near the project area by allowing them to vacate the area prior to the commencement of pile driving activities.

description: Pile driving activities for MET tower installation will be monitored by qualified marine mammal and sea turtle observers to ensure no individuals are present within the 7-kilometer exclusion zone.
geographic_scope: Area within 7 km of MET tower
context_quote: A preliminary 7 km radius exclusion zone for marine mammals and sea turtles must be established around each pile driving site in order to reduce the potential for impacts to these species.

description: Pile driving activities for MET tower installation will be halted if any marine mammals or sea turtles are observed within the 1-kilometer 180 dB exclusion zone.
geographic_scope: Area within 1 km of MET tower
context_quote: One observer must be based at or near the sound source and responsible for monitoring the 180 dB field of ensonification out to 1000m from the sound source.

description: The MET tower location will avoid areas with magnetic anomalies greater than 21 nT in amplitude.
context_quote: Nine small magnetic anomalies were detected within the MET tower APE. While there is no evidence that these features represent unexploded ordnance (UXO), these areas will be avoided during bottom-disturbing activities.

description: The MET tower will be decommissioned by either transporting it to an onshore disposal site, transporting it to an offshore artificial reef site, or abandoning it in place and transferring ownership to a scientific/educational institute.
context_quote: The process of decommissioning gives the developer a series of basic choices once the MET tower reaches its useful life in connection with the wind farm operation. These choices are as follows: 1) Decommission in accordance with BOEM regulations and transport to an on-shore licensed disposal site. 2) Decommission in accordance with BOEM regulations and transport to an offshore artificial reef site in agreement with the MD DNR or DE NREC artificial reef program. 3) Decommission by abandoning in place and transferring ownership for a nominal sum to a scientific/educational institute such as UMD or UDEL for in-situ research.
